question: For the frozen V56 SPCX cash-open long mechanism, do entry-anchored 40, 60, or 80 bps fixed targets reduce giveback and improve development robustness versus the unchanged prior-cash-close target under the same entries, stop, sizing, costs, and maximum hold?
why_now: The first prospective V56 long reached approximately 45 bps favorable excursion before retracing, while the frozen development long slice was positive in aggregate but negative after removing its largest winner. This is hypothesis formation, not evidence that the live exit is wrong.
selection_rule: highest count of positive stress development folds
highest worst stress development-fold net PnL
highest stress development net PnL excluding the largest winner
required_outputs: nominal and stress economics for the control and every challenger
all three chronological development folds without reselection
win/loss, profit factor, net PnL, net excluding largest winner, fees, funding, drawdown, and exit reasons
technical mark and executable-quote path resolution
no live strategy, risk, sizing, or configuration authority

interpretation_contract.minimum_forward_evidence_before_live_pro: At least one independently preregistered resolved long lifecycle under the selected challenger or a source-compatible shadow/canary comparison, with exact fees, slippage, target behavior, and no unresolved path evidence.

known_failure_modes: The candidate set was motivated after observing one open forward path, so it is not an untouched hypothesis.
A fixed target may reduce giveback while truncating the rare large recovery that drives the baseline long slice.
Development contains only nine baseline long trades and is regime-unstable across folds.
Earlier exits can change later capital availability; a long-only replay may not capture full shared-portfolio interaction.
Historical mark and quote gaps can make a scenario technically unresolved even when economics appear favorable.
A 15-minute bar establishes target touch but not exact within-bar queue priority beyond the simulator's conservative barrier ordering.
falsifier: Reject the fixed-target family if no challenger improves the preregistered stress fold and leave-largest criteria over the prior-close control, if entry identities diverge, if technical paths are unresolved, or if a forward source-compatible lifecycle demonstrates materially worse profit capture or costs. Do not update V56 from this development study alone.

evidence.role: first prospective long decision and initial protected lifecycle
